title: Phase 2 exit: dogfood ten outcomes through the spine, >=4 non-engineering and >=2 legal/compliance
description: Dogfood the spine by building this rebirth with it, under an explicit distribution quota: of the first ten outcomes run through the spine, at least four are non-engineering and at least two are legal- or compliance-flavored. The quota exists so the implication map is not tuned solely to the one distribution its author needs least. Phase 2 exit criterion. Note commitment 12: legal stays dogfood-only until a licensed attorney has reviewed its seed corpus and boundary behaviors.
acceptance_criteria: Ten real outcomes have run end to end through the spine, with the >=4 non-engineering and >=2 legal/compliance quota met and the distribution recorded.

title: Phase 2: decision inbox + cross-domain conflict framing
description: Work happens in the background; only decisions that are genuinely the user's surface. When one role says wait and another says ship, frame the tradeoff with both sides cited and put it in the inbox — no hidden precedence order and no heat-map auto-arbitration on judgment calls. Serves commitments 2 and 11. Built on the shared storage substrate.
acceptance_criteria: A cross-domain conflict produces a single inbox item framing both positions with citations; nothing auto-arbitrates a judgment call; non-decisions do not reach the inbox.
notes: 2026-08-03: storage (two-cited-positions rule enforced), kernel API, and 'construct inbox'/'construct decide' surface landed in bf4f4c8. Remaining: conflict DETECTION — turning two disagreeing roles into one framed inbox item needs the coordinator (r67.5).

title: Phase 2: work log — what was reviewed, what was flagged, what needs a licensed human
description: Invocation is invisible; accountability never is. Persist an append-only work log on the shared storage substrate recording what was done in each role's name. Serves commitment 4 and the no-fabrication trust kernel (commitment 15). Roles append via their scoped capability token only.
acceptance_criteria: Every role action taken during a run appears in the work log, including what was flagged and what was routed to a licensed human; the log is append-only and survives a crash mid-run.
notes: 2026-08-03: storage (append-only, trigger-enforced), kernel API, and 'construct log' surface landed in bf4f4c8. Remaining: entries for actual role execution (needs the coordinator, r67.5) — 'every role action' cannot be claimed until roles run.

title: Phase 2: kernel-owned capability tokens + dispatcher-owned completion transitions
description: draft -> challenged -> final is a dispatcher-owned transition triggered by recorded verdicts, never a tool a role can call on itself. A role holds a capability token scoped to its own run and task; it can submit drafts and append to the work log, and nothing else. Serves commitment 14, which exists because an ungated write surface let a role under completion pressure mark its own challenge passed — a verified live failure mode in the predecessor. Wire to the harvested completion ladder (src/kernel/completion/states.ts, ledger.ts). Kernel-owned MCP capability tokens are in scope.
acceptance_criteria: A role cannot advance its own completion state under test; attempts are rejected and logged. Tokens are scoped to a single run and task and grant only draft submission and work-log append.

title: Phase 2: bounded run coordinator — concurrency, leases, idempotency, spend ceiling
description: Make concurrent role execution crash-safe and cost-bounded. Explicitly a bounded coordinator, NOT an agent pool — STRATEGY calls a pool enterprise cosplay at this scale. Bounded concurrency, per-task rows on the SQLite substrate, leases so a crashed run is recoverable rather than wedged, idempotency so a resumed run does not duplicate work, and a global spend ceiling enforced in the coordinator. Serves Phase 2 program shape; the spend ceiling also serves STRATEGY risk 6 (cost outrunning a solo maintainer).
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent runs respect the concurrency bound; a killed process leaves recoverable leased tasks that resume without duplicating work; the global spend ceiling halts dispatch when reached.
close_reason: Coordinator, task rows with leases + fencing token, global spend ceiling. Verified live against OpenCode+ollama. Commit d418653

title: Phase 2: OpenCode host adapter — first-class, pinned and conformance-probed
description: Implement the OpenCode adapter behind the harvested host adapter interface (src/kernel/hosts/interface.ts), execute(role, task, tools) -> deliverable. Serves commitment 1: host-independent by adapter, never by rebuild. Pin the host version and run a conformance probe so a host upgrade surfaces as a failing probe rather than silent behavioral drift. Commitment 1 is a veto on reimplementing any host capability (STRATEGY risk 4, homebrew-runtime creep) — no own agent runtime, memory engine, or tool broker.
acceptance_criteria: OpenCode runs a real role task end to end through the adapter interface; the host version is pinned and a conformance probe fails when the pinned host's behavior changes.
notes:
2026-08-03 VERIFIED against a live OpenCode 1.15.4, not just unit-tested.

End to end through the adapter interface: createOpenCodeAdapter -> init() -> invoke({role:'privacy issue-spotter', task:'Read dpa.txt. Name the single biggest privacy risk in it, in one sentence.'}) returned status ok, one completed 'read' tool call, and a correct one-sentence deliverable naming the sub-processor discretion clause. Usage summed 24594 in / 126 out across 2 steps, cost 0 (local model).

Pin: PINNED_VERSION 1.15.4 in src/hosts/opencode/pin.ts, alongside 8 named behavioral expectations. scripts/probe-opencode-conformance.mjs checks all 8 against a live binary. Verified all three exit paths, not assumed: 0 with all 8 holding on the real host; 1 on version drift (proved with a shim reporting 9.9.9, which failed version-pinned and printed why it matters); 2 when no binary is reachable, so 'could not run' never reads as 'passed'.

Capturing fixtures from the real host corrected two claims I had written from a 2>&1 transcript: notices go to stderr (stdout under --format json is clean NDJSON), and a failed run DOES exit non-zero. Both were wrong in the first draft of pin.ts and are now recorded accurately. Kept the parser's non-JSON tolerance, documented as an accommodation for stream-merging callers rather than a host behavior.

Adapter lives in src/hosts/opencode/, which fills the exports['./hosts/*'] path r67.12 flagged. No host capability reimplemented (STRATEGY risk 4): no session store, retry policy, tool broker or model routing. Declares only 'interrupt' and 'concurrent'; 'stream' is deliberately NOT declared because the transcript is reduced after exit — our limitation, declared rather than hidden.

Unit tests found a real defect: on a timeout, kill() makes the child exit, so Promise.race between the child and the timer was a coin toss and a timed-out run could return ok. Fixed with an explicit expired flag checked after the race.

30 new tests (1096 -> 1126). Full gate green including the read-only-HOME sterile run and the packaged-install smoke.
close_reason: OpenCode adapter landed, verified end to end against a live host at the pinned version, with a conformance probe proven to fail on drift

title: Phase 2: brief schema + dispatcher satisfaction of declared requirements
description: A brief declares what a task needs: inputs, tool capabilities, verification postconditions. One dispatcher resolves those requirements against available tools (MCP connectors included) and roles. Serves commitment 10 — briefs declare, a dispatcher satisfies; briefs do not orchestrate themselves. Extends the harvested src/kernel/routing/dispatcher.ts and reuses src/kernel/capabilities/postconditions.ts; do not add a second dispatcher.
acceptance_criteria: A brief schema with inputs, tool capabilities, and verification postconditions; the dispatcher resolves a brief against available tools and roles and fails loudly on an unsatisfiable requirement rather than silently degrading.
close_reason: Brief schema + dispatcher satisfaction; unsatisfiable briefs fail loudly

title: Phase 2: implication map — outcome to implicated domains, with a measured miss-rate gate
description: Decompose a stated outcome into the domains it implicates (privacy law, commerce/tax, program sequencing, product scoping) without the user naming any of them. Serves commitment 1 and is the head of the Phase 2 spine (outcome -> implication map -> dispatch -> host adapter -> deliverable). STRATEGY risk 1 requires this be MEASURED, not assumed: build a labeled outcome set with a pre-agreed miss-rate target and gate on it, otherwise the whole vision is a routing demo. Builds on the harvested intake classifier (src/kernel/intake/classify.ts) rather than a second classification path.
acceptance_criteria: A labeled outcome set exists with a written, pre-agreed miss-rate target; the implication map runs against it in CI and fails the build when the miss rate regresses past the target.
close_reason: Implication map + measured gate: miss 0.000 (target 0.15), over 0.098 (target 0.60)

title: Phase 2: build the tracker projection storage substrate
description: Deferred here from construct-cpz. The pure projection + field-authority logic is already harvested into src/kernel/tracker/ (authority.ts, projection.ts), dual-run locked against v2 and clock-free. What remains is STORAGE, which is a rewrite rather than a port: v2 persisted projections through a Dolt lock. Build it on the same substrate Phase 2's spine needs for the work log and decision inbox, so one storage shape serves all three consumers instead of the harvest guessing at one before its consumer exists. Also port lib/tracker-projection/reconcile.mjs at that point — reconciliation is where field authority earns its keep (a domain-owned field is never overwritten by the tracker and vice versa), and it is only testable against real persisted state.
acceptance_criteria: A storage substrate serving projections, work log, and decision inbox; reconcile ported on top of it with the field-authority rule enforced and tested.
close_reason: Substrate built (src/kernel/store/) + reconcile ported (src/kernel/tracker/reconcile.ts), field authority enforced through persisted state. 287a6ed

title: Phase 1: Port `construct cleanup` — v2 trace detection + removal, fixture-home verified
description: Port the detection catalog from construct-legacy's lib/uninstall/uninstall.mjs + lib/maintenance/cleanup.mjs into src/kernel + a `cleanup` CLI command, adapted to v3's no-ambient-fs-outside-paths.ts discipline and sterile test harness. Catalog covers project scope (.construct/, construct-authored .claude/ entries, .mcp.json, .gitignore append, git hooksPath) and machine scope (~/.construct/, ~/.cache/construct/, construct entries in ~/.claude.json, XDG state/cache dirs). Verify against a fixture home built from a real predecessor install (not only synthetic fixtures) per STRATEGY's Phase 1 exit criterion. This is the phase's alpha-gating deliverable: STRATEGY says it is 'the only backward obligation' and 'ships in the first 0.x alpha.' Progress 2026-08-03: filesystem + git-config traces are ported and shipped (src/kernel/cleanup/{catalog,run}.ts, wired as `construct cleanup` in src/cli/index.ts) — project launcher, manifested agents/commands, settings.json/.mcp.json un-merge, .construct/ state, scaffold files, git core.hooksPath, XDG state/data/cache dirs, config.env, lib symlink, postgres compose file, and memory-MCP registrations across Claude/OpenCode/Codex — verified against both a synthetic fixture home (tests/kernel/cleanup/catalog.test.ts, tests/cli/cleanup.test.ts) and, read-only via `npm run smoke`'s new `construct cleanup --dry-run` step, this machine's real accumulated construct-legacy state. Docker container/image removal and the macOS LaunchAgent unload are NOT ported (split out to construct-506.1.1) — this issue stays open until that lands or is explicitly descoped.
close_reason: The 506.1.1 split (Docker container/image + LaunchAgent removal) landed, closing the only remaining gap this issue was held open for. construct cleanup now covers the full v2 detection catalog -- project scope (launcher, agents/commands manifests, settings.json/.mcp.json un-merge, .construct/ state, scaffold files, git core.hooksPath) and machine scope (XDG state/data/cache dirs, config.env, lib symlink, postgres compose file + container removal, LaunchAgent, memory-MCP registrations across Claude/OpenCode/Codex, opt-in pgvector image) -- verified against both a synthetic fixture home and (read-only via npm run smoke) this machine's real accumulated state. Fixture-home + injectable-spawn tests cover every category; full suite (27/27), typecheck, lint, build, and smoke all green.

title: Phase 1: Release pipeline + publish first 0.x alpha
description: Add a publish workflow (none exists yet — v3's .github/workflows only has ci.yml) gated on 506.1's cleanup command landing. Tag and publish @geraldmaron/construct-engine's first 0.x alpha per the revised version lineage (STRATEGY: starting at 0.0.0, no stability promise until the Phase 5 second-user gate). Closes Phase 1's 'ships in the first 0.x alpha' exit criterion.
notes:
2026-08-03 attempt. NPM_TOKEN secret IS now set on geraldmaron/construct, pulled from 1Password item 'npm' (geralddagher-development vault) — the item whose own note names this exact purpose. Tag v0.0.0 cut and pushed; release.yml ran and every gate step passed (lint, typecheck, 997 tests, smoke, tag/version match). PUBLISH FAILED: npm error E404 on PUT @geraldmaron/construct-engine.

Diagnosed, not guessed: that token is a GRANULAR token scoped to the single package @geraldmaron/construct (read+write), exactly as its 1Password note says. Proof — authed GET of @geraldmaron/construct returns 200, but GET /-/user/geraldmaron/package returns 'You may not perform that action with these credentials', and @geraldmaron/construct-engine does not exist (anonymous GET 404). npm returns 404 rather than 403 when a token may not CREATE a package, so E404 here means 'not allowed to create', not 'missing'.

Reusing the token's package is not an option: @geraldmaron/construct is the live v2 package (48 versions, latest 2.1.1, published 2026-07-31). v3 is deliberately a new package name.

BLOCKED ON GERALD — needs a token that can create @geraldmaron/construct-engine: on npmjs.com mint a granular access token covering @geraldmaron/construct-engine (or the whole @geraldmaron scope) with read+write, then update the NPM_TOKEN repo secret. Minting it requires signing in to npmjs.com, which an agent must not do.

Then no re-tag is needed — re-run the failed release run (gh run rerun 30860594816) and it publishes. Tag v0.0.0 is left in place for that. Note: a provenance attestation was signed to the public sigstore transparency log (logIndex 2337573251) before the registry rejected the publish; it attests a build, not a published package, and is harmless.

Pushed to github.com/geraldmaron/construct (main), CI run 30856478400 fully green.

title: Reconcile commitment 14's draft/challenged/final with the harvested 12-rung completion ladder
description: Two different ladders are being treated as one. STRATEGY commitments 13 and 14 name a three-state, dispatcher-owned transition: draft -> challenged -> final. The harvested code has no such states — src/kernel/completion/states.ts is v2's twelve-rung deliverable-production ladder (planned, authored, structurally-valid, source-linted, exported, file-valid, renderable, screenshot-captured, visually-reviewed, accessibility-reviewed, approved, completed), and grep for 'challenged' across src/ returns zero hits. src/kernel/brief/schema.ts:39 already writes 'before promoting past draft' in a comment against a ladder with no draft rung.\n\nr67.6's acceptance criteria says to wire the capability tokens to states.ts and ledger.ts, which cannot be done as literally written. Resolve before r67.6 starts: either the three states are a coarser gate layered above the twelve rungs (challenged maps to a rung range), or the twelve-rung ladder is deliverable-production detail and commitment 14 governs a separate promotion state, or the ladder is amended. Serves commitments 13, 14 and 16 — an unstated conflict between STRATEGY and the harvested kernel is exactly the drift commitment 16 exists to surface.
acceptance_criteria: One written decision states how draft/challenged/final relates to COMPLETION_STATES; whichever way it resolves, STRATEGY, the ladder, and r67.6's acceptance criteria agree, and no comment references a state the code does not have.

title: Packaged-install smoke must exercise the spine, not just doctor/version/cleanup
description: scripts/smoke-packaged-install.sh still tests only the Phase 0/1 surface (doctor, version, cleanup --dry-run). The spine commands added in bf4f4c8 — outcome, log, inbox, decide — are untested from a packaged install, and they are the only code path that opens node:sqlite and writes to the state dir. That is precisely the packaging-defect class the script's own header says it exists to catch. Verified 2026-08-03 that 'construct outcome' DOES work from a real npm-packed install today, so this is a missing guard, not a live defect — but nothing stops the next dist/ or files[] change from breaking it silently. Serves STRATEGY Phase 0 (packaged-install smoke) extended to the Phase 2 surface.
acceptance_criteria: The smoke script runs outcome, log, inbox and decide against a packaged install with an isolated HOME, asserts the run is recorded and read back, and fails if the spine cannot open its store from the tarball.

title: Run the repo's own gate before a commit lands, not after the push
description: main went red at cddf718 (CI run 30862753238) because bf4f4c8 introduced a glossary violation in src/kernel/run/outcome.ts. Nothing local caught it: core.hooksPath points at .beads/hooks, whose pre-commit only exports beads, and .claude/settings.json wires only scripts/hooks/no-fabrication-lint.mjs. CI is therefore the first and only gate, and it runs after the push. Serves STRATEGY Phase 0 ('a minimal fail-open hook set') and commitment 16 — a red main makes every subsequent CI signal unreadable, which is exactly the drift the self-monitoring commitment exists to catch. Fail-open per Phase 0: the gate warns and never wedges a commit.
acceptance_criteria: A commit that would fail 'npm run lint' or 'npm run typecheck' is surfaced locally before it is pushed; the check is fail-open (a broken or missing hook never blocks a commit) and coexists with the beads pre-commit hook rather than replacing it.

title: Phase 2 exit: one external person runs one real outcome
description: One external person runs one real outcome end to end through the spine. Phase 2 exit criterion, and a standing obligation for every phase after this one. This is the first evidence that the outcome-in/decisions-out surface works for someone who did not build it.
acceptance_criteria: One person who did not build Construct has run one real outcome to a delivered result; their friction points are filed as issues.

title: Phase 2: Claude Agent SDK adapter at smoke parity with OpenCode
description: Second adapter behind the same interface, proving host independence is real rather than asserted. Serves commitment 1. Scope is smoke parity with the OpenCode adapter, not feature parity: the same smoke task produces an equivalent deliverable through both hosts.
acceptance_criteria: The same smoke task runs through both the OpenCode and Agent SDK adapters and produces an equivalent deliverable; divergence fails the smoke.

title: Phase 1: cleanup — Docker container/image + macOS LaunchAgent removal
description: Port the two categories from construct-legacy's lib/uninstall/uninstall.mjs that construct-506.1 explicitly deferred: stopping/removing the local Postgres Docker container (+ optional --with-images pgvector image removal) and unloading + removing the macOS pressure-release LaunchAgent plist. Both require spawning a live external process (docker, launchctl) rather than a filesystem check, so they need an injectable spawn dependency to stay unit-testable rather than the fixture-home approach used for the rest of the catalog. Until this lands, `construct cleanup` prints an explicit coverage-gap note rather than silently omitting them.
close_reason: Ported both categories from construct-legacy's uninstall.mjs: machine-postgres-container (stop+rm+volume for both the per-home-namespaced name and the legacy singular 'construct-postgres', risk=ask) and machine-launchagent (launchctl bootout+unload then plist removal, risk=auto, darwin-gated). Both take an injectable spawn (CleanupTarget.spawn) and platform (CleanupTarget.platform) so tests fake docker/launchctl instead of depending on real machine state -- generic fixture tests updated to inject a not-found fake spawn so they stay sterile regardless of host docker state. Also added the --with-images opt-in for the pgvector image removal (machine-pgvector-image, risk=ask) and threaded --with-images through the CLI. Removed the CLEANUP_COVERAGE_NOTE from cli/index.ts since both named gaps are now covered. 4 new unit tests in catalog.test.ts (postgres container dual-name removal, --with-images gating, launchagent darwin-gated detect+remove, launchagent non-darwin no-op) plus a spawn-override hook threaded through cli/index.ts's cleanup() and cleanup.test.ts so CLI-level tests stay deterministic too. typecheck, lint, full test suite (27/27), build, and npm run smoke (real packaged install against this machine's actual XDG state) all green.

title: Phase 1: Harvest dual-run-leaf kernel modules (classification, postconditions, completion ladder, host adapter interface)
description: Port as pure libraries under src/kernel/, no CLI/repo assumptions, tests carried over behind the sterile harness as behavior-locked (dual-run) tests: outcome classification + routing (construct-legacy lib/intake/classify.mjs, lib/skills/router.mjs), brief postcondition validation (lib/capabilities/postconditions.mjs), the deliverable completion ladder (lib/artifact-completion.mjs, lib/artifact-completion-states.mjs), and the multi-host sync seam / adapter interface (lib/runtime/contract/interface.mjs + adapters). Each module ships with its own ported test suite proving parity with legacy behavior before any v3-only extension. No-fabrication enforcement beyond v3's existing tier-1 claims.ts is not carried over here — legacy has no systematic untagged-claim checker beyond what's already ported.
close_reason: Ported classification+preset tables, route scoring, postconditions, completion ladder, and the host adapter seam into src/kernel/ as pure libraries. Behavior-locked against captured predecessor output (scripts/capture-legacy-*.mjs freeze what v2 actually returned; the frozen JSON is what CI asserts). Full gate green: 197 tests, typecheck, lint, build, packaged smoke. Two field renames (contractStart->briefStart, evidence.artifact->evidence.deliverable) per the glossary, with the capture scripts translating so the dual run compares behavior not vocabulary; rule ids left untouched. Follow-up construct-egc filed for the rdStage vocabulary. Fixed (616e13a).

title: OpenCode's first-run database migration is not concurrency-safe
description: A live run of 'construct work --concurrency=2' against a fresh OpenCode data dir failed one of three tasks: the concurrent invocations raced OpenCode's own one-time sqlite migration ('Performing one time database migration, may take a few minutes...' then exit 1). The adapter declares the 'concurrent' capability, which is true for session state but not for the host's first-run migration. Options: warm the host once in init() before allowing concurrent invokes, or record the limitation as a named expectation in src/hosts/opencode/pin.ts so the conformance probe checks it. Found while landing construct-r67.5.
acceptance_criteria: A first run at concurrency>1 against a fresh OpenCode data dir does not fail any task, or the limitation is declared and probed rather than hit at runtime.

title: package.json declares an exports path and a files entry that nothing builds

The export is aspirational: src/kernel/hosts/interface.ts says in its own header that an adapter is host-coupled and belongs outside the kernel boundary, which is what './hosts/*' was reserved for. Serves commitment 1 (host-independent by adapter) — where the first adapter physically lives is r67.3's opening decision, and this stays broken until r67.3 either fills src/hosts/ or the export is dropped.
acceptance_criteria: Every path in exports[] resolves from a packaged install, or is removed; files[] lists no directory that the tarball does not contain.
notes: 2026-08-03 resolved as part of r67.3. src/hosts/opencode/ now exists, so exports['./hosts/*'] resolves: verified from a real npm-packed install that @geraldmaron/construct-engine/hosts/opencode/index.js, the root export, and kernel/hosts/interface.js all import cleanly. Removed 'packs' from files[] — it does not exist yet and contributed 0 entries to the tarball; it can return when Phase 4 builds packs.

title: Decide owner for the tracker substrate (Phase 1 harvest vs Phase 2 spine)
description: Split out of construct-506.3, which explicitly said to re-evaluate this before starting. The predecessor's lib/tracker-projection/*.mjs holds portable projection + field-authority logic, but its storage is a dolt lock that has to be REWRITTEN on a SQLite substrate rather than ported. That rewrite is the same substrate Phase 2's spine needs for the work log and decision inbox, so building it inside the Phase 1 harvest risks committing to a storage shape before the consumer that defines its requirements exists. Neither item gates the Phase 1 alpha publish (per STRATEGY only cleanup does). Decide: build the substrate now under Phase 1, or defer it to Phase 2 and harvest only the pure projection/field-authority logic here.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision, and either a Phase 1 implementation bead or a Phase 2 dependency link.

title: Reconcile v2 rdStage vocabulary with the glossary
description: The ported intake tables (src/kernel/intake/tables/) carry v2 rdStage values, one of which is 'artifact' — a term the glossary retires in favor of 'deliverable'. It cannot be renamed as part of construct-506.2 because rdStage flows into classifier output that is behavior-locked by tests/kernel/intake/fixtures/classify-golden.json, so a rename is a behavior change, not a rename. The tables directory is currently exempted in scripts/lint-glossary-parity.mjs (with the reason inline). Decide whether the stage vocabulary is v3 vocabulary that should be renamed (and the golden corpus re-baselined with the diff explained), or v2 corpus data that stays frozen — then either do the rename or narrow the lint exemption to keywords only.
acceptance_criteria: Either the rdStage vocabulary is renamed and the golden corpus re-baselined with an explained diff, or the exemption in scripts/lint-glossary-parity.mjs is narrowed to match-keywords only and the decision is recorded.
close_reason: DECIDED: rename, not exempt. rdStage 'artifact' -> 'deliverable' (a stage name is Construct's own vocabulary; the glossary binds every surface). The lint exemption is narrowed from the whole tables directory to blanking 'keywords: [...]' arrays only — match keywords are the words USERS write in their documents and renaming them would break classification. Verified by reintroducing the stage name and confirming the lint fails. The captured golden corpus was NOT rewritten: it stays a faithful record of v2 (capture still reproduces it byte-for-byte, checksum confirmed) and the intentional divergence is declared in the test. Fixed (0e99f91).
